text:
Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for agreeing to evaluate this 21-year-old male who presented to my clinic for a general check-up. He is a full-time university student with no active medical complaints. His family history is unremarkable, and he takes no prescription medications.

Physical examination reveals a distinctly circular facial profile with auricles that are positioned noticeably low relative to the intercanthal line. An oral examination shows markedly reduced tooth size throughout his dentition, and review of his panoramic dental films demonstrates congenital agenesis of multiple permanent teeth, specifically seven missing adult teeth. A targeted inspection of his anterior teeth revealed no accessory cingulum cusps. 

His extremities are notable for structural variations in both hands. His thumbs exhibit striking hyperextension and hyperabduction, creating a pronounced Z-like deformity. There is also clear medial curvature of the fifth digits bilaterally, and previous imaging shows an extra phalanx within his index and middle digits. 

The remainder of his physical examination was thoroughly normal, including clear lung sounds, normal heart sounds without murmurs, an unremarkable abdominal exam, and fully intact peripheral neurological function. Routine laboratory studies, including a complete blood count and comprehensive metabolic panel, showed no abnormalities.

I would appreciate your expert evaluation regarding his physical and dental features to help clarify his presentation and advise on any necessary follow-up.

Sincerely,
Dr. Julian Vance
